candidates: Apply conditional or state-dependent CSS through Emotion `styled()` (imported from `storybook/theming`) rather than inline `style` props. Inline styles obscure which rules apply under which conditions and bypass the Emotion theming pipeline.

When adding props to an Emotion `styled` component that are purely for styling (not intended as HTML attributes), prefix them with `$` (e.g., `$isActive`, `$isInitialValue`). This prevents Emotion from forwarding them to the DOM element and signals to readers that the prop drives styles only.

When a UI control should be hidden but must still occupy its layout space (to avoid width/height shifts), use `visibility: hidden` (or `opacity: 0`) via a styled component rather than conditionally rendering `null` or `undefined`. Add `aria-hidden={true}` alongside so assistive technology correctly skips the invisible element.
